# Certified CPU controller, version 3

Extend the supplied FENIX CPU controller. Its model evaluators classify nine-packet length/IPD windows, its control-plane compiler builds a sampled probability table, and its reporting code aggregates window predictions into flows. Implement joint certified export planning between these stages. The fixed model assets are part of the contract, not a training task. Reserved service opportunities abstract the inference/link pipeline; this is an offline controller extension and makes no hardware-timing or learned-accuracy reproduction claim.

## Input

The entry is `python3 -B /workspace/submission/main.py`, cwd /workspace. Read exactly one UTF-8 JSON object to EOF. Keys must be unique at every depth. Reject invalid UTF-8, trailing JSON, nonfinite numbers, booleans/decimal/exponent values in integer fields, unknown/missing keys, depth over64 containers, and every schema violation below. Input is at most16MiB. Invalid input returns exactly `{"error":"invalid"}` and exits0, with no partial results. Valid input returns `{"version":3,"results":[RESULT,...]}` in case order. Object order/whitespace are irrelevant; arrays have the specified order and JSON types are exact except for the report scalar number equivalence stated below.

Top-level keys: exactly `version,cases`. Version is integer3. cases has0–8 epochs; at most1024 total windows across the batch. Each epoch has exactly `model,class_values,stats,bucket,slots,flows,groups,windows`:

| Field | Meaning and bounds |
|---|---|
| model | exactly the string `cnn` or `rnn`, selecting the corresponding bundled seven-class model |
| class_values | seven integer utilities1–1000, indexed by predicted class |
| stats | `[N,Q,V]`, positive integers ≤10^9: global observations supplied to `probability.calculate_probability_model(Q,N,V)`; the table compiler converts its elapsed-time samples by dividing by1000 |
| bucket | `[B,I]`: capacity1–512 tokens, initial0–B |
| slots |1–256 rows `[time,capacity,refill]`: strictly increasing integer times0–10^12; service capacity0–512; refill0–512; first refill must be0 |
| flows |1–32 rows `[target,ceiling,group,label]`: target1–64, ceiling target–512; group=-1 or a group index; fixed true class label0–6 |
| groups |0–32 rows `[parent,ceiling]`: parent=-1 or a group index; parent links must be acyclic, in any input order; ceiling0–512 |
| windows |0–512 rows `[flow,ready,expires,T,C,draw,priority,features]`: flow is a zero-based flow index; ready0–10^12, expires ready–10^12; T1–65535, C1–320; draw0–65535; priority1–1000; features exactly nine `[length,IPD]` integer rows, length0–1500 and IPD0–2560, oldest first |

Each window row is a distinct indivisible candidate, identified by its input index. `ready` includes feature formation and fixed transfer lead time; `expires` is its last permitted export opportunity after accounting for the reserved inference pipeline. T and C are measured age and packet backlog from a preceding frozen observation period; choosing a window does not change another window's T,C. Any window may be assigned at most once, to a slot with ready≤time≤expires, and only if it passes its gate. Each flow receives at most its ceiling. A group limits the total selected windows of every flow attached to it or any descendant; all ancestor ceilings apply simultaneously. Group=-1 means no group; parent=-1 means a root. Groups may have no attached flows. These are explicit control-epoch resource policies; they are not classification labels. There is no required order among windows of the same flow and no extra FIFO constraint: slots are reserved service opportunities, not a simulation queue.

## Model predictions, compiled gates and finite tokens

For every window, including ones later rejected, run the selected evaluator's `evaluate_model_single_pass` on its features. The bundled `testcnnonnx.py`, `testrnnonnx.py`, `data_loader_npy.py`, assets and NumPy1.26.4/ONNX Runtime1.16.3 CPU path define the prediction primitive. Use one-window inference and the supplied one-thread sequential session settings. Its integer output is the lowest class index attaining the maximum first model output. CNN output is shape(1,7); RNN's shape(7) is intentional. No other model, training, randomized approximation or accelerator is needed. Window j has exact integer value priority_j*class_values[prediction_j]. These values affect planning; true labels affect only reports.

Compile the table once per epoch with the supplied `probability.calculate_probability_model(Q,N,V)`. Its published code, including the20x20 binary64 sampled grid, elapsed-time /1000 conversion, clipping, equality tolerance and floor-to65535 conversion, is the normative primitive. Look up the unique row whose inclusive elapsed and count ranges contain T,C; its last integer is the window threshold (default0 if no row). `window_thresholds` implements this lookup. A window passes exactly when draw<threshold. A threshold65535 rejects draw65535. Do not substitute an unsampled continuous formula or a different rounding rule. The public compiler is supplied and need not be reimplemented. Selected windows each consume one token and one service unit.

Initially I tokens are available at the first slot. At every later slot, add that slot's refill and discard tokens above B before allocating exports. Exports at a slot cannot exceed its service capacity or available tokens; unspent tokens carry to the next slot. No refill occurs between slots. Token sources may be unused: using an earlier available token instead of a later one has no objective advantage. Saturation can make a total-epoch token budget insufficient as a feasibility test.

## Objective and output

Let n_f be the number of chosen windows of flow f, and t_f its target. Coverage is r=min(1,min_f(n_f/t_f)). First maximize r. Among those allocations maximize U, the sum of chosen values. Among those minimize A, the sum of (assigned slot time-ready) for chosen windows. All ties are allowed; do not invent a tie-break. Even when r=0, the later objectives apply. An empty selection is always feasible, so every valid epoch has a solution.

A RESULT has exactly `predictions,reports,ratio,thresholds,assignment,utility,age,flow,potential,cut`:

- predictions contains one class0–6 per input window in input order.
- reports is `metrics.selected_report(flows,windows,predictions,assignment)` as specified below.
- ratio is `[p,q]` in lowest terms, 0≤p≤q≤64, q≥1, expressing optimal r.
- thresholds contains one exact threshold per input window.
- assignment contains one slot index or -1 per input window.
- utility and age are exact U,A.
- flow, potential, cut are the certificates defined next. They are required, not optional claims by the program.

## Selected-window reports

Report exactly `{"packet":METRICS,"stream":METRICS}`. Packet labels are the true flow label and predicted class of each selected window. A stream is a flow with at least one selected window; its predicted label is the most frequent selected-window class, breaking count ties by the earliest selected window in **input order**, independent of service order. Its true label is that flow's fixed label. No unselected window or unrepresented flow contributes to either report.

METRICS has exactly `confusion,accuracy,macro_precision,macro_recall,macro_f1`. Confusion is a7x7 integer matrix with true labels as rows and predicted labels as columns. For each class, precision=TP/(TP+FP), recall=TP/(TP+FN), F1=2TP/(2TP+FP+FN), with zero for a zero denominator. Macro metrics average **all seven** classes, including absent classes. Accuracy is correct/total, or0 for an empty sample. Empty reports contain an all-zero confusion matrix and four zeros. The supplied metric routines implement these semantics and include empty-set handling. The four scalar metrics may use integer, decimal or exponent JSON number notation (for example1,1.0,1e0 are equivalent); booleans are not numbers. After standard Python JSON decoding, their values must be finite and within absolute1e-9 of the mathematical values, with no relative tolerance. Confusion and every other integer field remain exact JSON integers; decimal/exponent notation is not valid there. These reports describe selected classifications, not the optimization objective.

## Certificate coordinate system

This defines a constraint network solely to make certificates machine-checkable; no solver, graph constructor or optimizer is supplied. Let S,J,F,G be slot, window, flow and group counts. Node0 is a token source R; node1 a completion sink Z. For each slot s, nodes a_s=2+3s, b_s=3+3s, e_s=4+3s represent token intake, capped inventory and reserved service. Window j has node w_j=2+3S+j. Flow f has node z_f=2+3S+J+f. Group g has node h_g=2+3S+J+F+g. There are K=2+3S+J+F+G nodes. Let W=1+J*(last slot time). Every arc has lower0/cost0 unless specified. Construct the following ordered arc list; omit no zero-capacity arc:

1. For each slot s in order: R→a_s has capacity I for s=0, otherwise refill_s; a_s→b_s capacity B; if s+1<S, b_s→a_(s+1) capacity B; b_s→e_s capacity capacity_s. Within a slot use this stated order.
2. For every eligible (slot s,window j), in slot-major then window-index order, e_s→w_j has capacity1 and cost `(time_s-ready_j)-value_j*W`. Eligible means the window passes and ready_j≤time_s≤expires_j.
3. For each window j in order: w_j→z_(flow_j), capacity1.
4. For each flow f in order: z_f→h_(group_f), or z_f→Z if group=-1, lower ceil(r*target_f), capacity ceiling_f.
5. For each group g in order: h_g→h_(parent_g), or h_g→Z if parent=-1, capacity ceiling_g.
6. Z→R, capacity J.

A `flow` is an integer for every arc in this order, within its lower/capacity bounds, conserving flow at every node. An eligible-pair arc has flow1 exactly when assignment[j]=s; an unassigned window has none. Utility/age and r must agree with the assignment and objective. Any valid token provenance may be used; no particular carry/refill decomposition is required.

`potential` has one mathematical integer per node, each with absolute value ≤10^60. For every arc (u,v,l,h,c) with reported amount x, require c+potential[u]-potential[v]≥0 if x<h, and -c+potential[v]-potential[u]≥0 if x>l. No condition is imposed in a direction with no residual capacity. These inequalities certify the optimum of the final two objectives at the reported coverage. W makes one utility unit dominate the entire possible waiting-age range; it is a certificate cost convention, not a runtime or scoring threshold. Potentials need not be unique or normalized.

For maximal coverage, define the finite public set Rset={k/target_f: f ranges over flows, k=0..target_f}. The reported r must belong to this set. If r=1, cut must be null. Otherwise let r+ be the smallest Rset member strictly larger than r. Use the same arc list but replace each flow lower bound by ceil(r+*target_f). `cut` is a list of distinct node IDs describing a subset X for which **sum of lower bounds on arcs entering X exceeds sum of capacities on arcs leaving X**. Arcs wholly inside/outside do not contribute. This is an infeasibility obstruction for the next larger coverage; any such set, in any order, is accepted. A result must satisfy both the allocation and its certificates; a locally plausible allocation or an unproved objective is insufficient.

The public check supplies no allocation optimizer, objective evaluator or graph/certificate evaluator. It checks a tiny static result and JSON/CLI behavior. All constraints and the full domain above are normative.

# Submission and runtime boundaries

Submit a regular directory `submission/` with a regular UTF-8 `main.py`. Supporting modules, data and subdirectories are allowed: at most8MiB total regular-file bytes and256 entries including directories. Symlinks, multiply-linked files and special files are rejected for collection safety. NumPy1.26.4, ONNX Runtime1.16.3 and their pinned dependencies are bundled under /workspace/vendor; native runtime libraries are under /workspace/native. No download, training or native compilation is needed. Standard-library, bundled-package and submitted-module imports are allowed. Only frozen submission bytes are executed; editing public runner/checker/protocol files does not affect verification. The task provides CPython 3.11.14 on Linux x86-64, CPU only.

Each invocation handles the **whole** batch within 150 seconds wall time. Local worker limits are 180 CPU seconds soft /181 hard per process, 2 GiB address space per process, 64 processes/threads per reserved UID for the outer generic worker; the candidate child itself is restricted to one process/one thread by the public runner, 256 open descriptors per process, 64 MiB per regular file, zero core dumps. The inherited generic worker uses at most its first two available CPUs (no exclusive cores). Input ≤16 MiB, stdout ≤32 MiB, stderr ≤1 MiB. Limits apply to errors too; output overflow, empty/non-JSON/wrong output, nonzero exit, or timeout fails the invocation. A normal zero exit, including `os._exit(0)`, is accepted only if complete correct JSON actually reaches the stdout pipe. Text stdin/stdout, .buffer, raw descriptors 0/1, fileno(), and fdopen() all work. The public checker executes a separate bounded child and checks its actual bytes and exit status.

The local trial runs as a nonprivileged reserved UID in an allowlisted chroot with immutable runtime/source and clean environment. Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable and is cleared between invocations; it need not be used. Runtime files and standard `/dev/null`, `/dev/zero`, `/dev/random`, `/dev/urandom` are available; only a read-only /proc/cpuinfo CPU-descriptor snapshot is exposed (needed by the bundled inference runtime); no process /proc entries, /sys, credentials, private verifier, or solution is mounted. Networking (including loopback) is disabled. Socket/socketpair/connect; System V shared memory/semaphore/message queues; kill/tkill/tgkill; ptrace/process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev; unshare/setns; mount/umount2/pivot_root/chroot; setsid/setpgid; identity/group changes; open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at; bpf; keyctl/add_key/request_key; perf_event_open; userfaultfd; io_uring operations; and pidfd_getfd are denied with EPERM. The outer generic filter marks clone3 unavailable; the candidate runner returns EPERM for clone3, as observed in the actual child profile. Namespace-creating clone flags are denied. The candidate runner additionally denies fork, vfork, clone and clone3, so a candidate cannot create subprocesses/threads. Its parent can still launch the candidate and cleanly reap it. The runner also independently denies socket/socketpair/connect, kill/tkill/tgkill, ptrace, process_vm_readv/process_vm_writev, pidfd_open and pidfd_send_signal in the candidate child; its parent retains pidfd-based cleanup. The outer profile supplies the remaining listed restrictions. Non-x86-64 and x32 syscall ABIs are terminated. No resources outside this contract are necessary.

The worker sets PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, HOME=/workspace, LANG=LC_ALL=C, TMPDIR=/workspace/tmp, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, PYTHONHASHSEED=0, LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/workspace/native, and OpenBLAS/OMP/MKL thread counts to 1. Source is run with -B; no site customization is submitted. Scratch is monitored approximately every 0.25 seconds: >1 GiB max(logical,allocated) file bytes or >50000 path entries triggers an **infrastructure error with no score**, not a precise quota. This local profile has no hard aggregate cgroup CPU/memory/storage guarantee and shares the host kernel. It is a local development/trial profile, not proof of hostile-kernel isolation. Formal container/transport validation remains pending separately.

`python3 public_check.py [--candidate PATH]` uses only this public workspace. Run it inside the supplied container or equivalent unprivileged development environment. It is a sanity checker and does not establish isolation by itself. It sets the same child resource limits, wall/output bounds and no-fork/no-socket filter without root; an outer container or worker supplies filesystem/UID and the remaining syscall restrictions. `python3 public_exec.py PATH` uses the same bounded child and relays its actual output/exit for local grading. Descendant creation is prevented, not left to an unbounded process-tree scan. It returns nonzero for candidate failure and never writes a reward. The private formal verifier is a separate image and remains fail-closed pending infrastructure validation. Runtime is a feasibility budget, not an optimization score or hardware-performance metric.

Native libraries use the bundled Ubuntu20.04 x86-64 libstdc++/libgcc10.5.0 and zlib1.2.11 copies; no native library path outside the public runtime is required.

The public runner observes SIGTERM/SIGINT during both pipe transfer and the final process-exit wait, including when the child has closed all pipes but stays alive. """CPU probability-table compiler and range lookup."""
import numpy as np

def calculate_probability_model(pkt_count, flow_count, feature_rate=75):
    
    N = flow_count if flow_count > 0 else 1
    V = feature_rate
    Q = pkt_count if pkt_count > 0 else 1
    
    threshold_NV = N / V
    threshold_QN = Q / N
    
    T_min, T_max = 1, 65535
    C_min, C_max = 1, 320
    num_samples_per_axis = 20 
    sample_T = np.linspace(T_min, T_max, num_samples_per_axis)
    sample_C = np.linspace(C_min, C_max, num_samples_per_axis)
    probability_table_data = []
    T_step = (T_max - T_min) // num_samples_per_axis
    C_step = (C_max - C_min) // num_samples_per_axis
    
    for i, T_i in enumerate(sample_T):
        for j, C_i in enumerate(sample_C):
            T_i_us = T_i / 1000
            Q_i = C_i / T_i_us
            P_i = 0
            if abs(C_i - (Q / N) * T_i_us) < 1e-3:
                P_i = 1 if T_i_us >= threshold_NV else 0
            elif C_i < (Q / N) * T_i_us:
                denominator1 = Q * T_i_us - N * C_i
                if denominator1 != 0 and T_i_us >= threshold_NV:
                    numerator1 = C_i * (V * T_i_us - N)
                    P_i = numerator1 / denominator1
            else:
                denominator2 = N * C_i - Q * T_i_us
                if denominator2 != 0 and V * C_i >= Q:
                    numerator2 = T_i_us * (V * C_i - Q)
                    P_i = numerator2 / denominator2
            P_i = max(0, min(1, P_i))
            T_low = int(T_min + i * T_step)
            T_high = int(T_min + (i + 1) * T_step - 1) if i < num_samples_per_axis - 1 else T_max
            C_low = int(C_min + j * C_step)
            C_high = int(C_min + (j + 1) * C_step - 1) if j < num_samples_per_axis - 1 else C_max
            
            prob_int = int(P_i * 65535)
            
            probability_table_data.append([1, T_low, T_high, C_low, C_high, prob_int])
    
    return probability_table_data

def window_thresholds(stats, windows):
    n, q, v = stats
    rows = calculate_probability_model(q, n, v)
    answer = []
    for window in windows:
        elapsed, packets = window[3], window[4]
        answer.append(next((int(row[5]) for row in rows
            if row[1] <= elapsed <= row[2] and row[3] <= packets <= row[4]), 0))
    return answer

"""Packet and flow classification reports, including empty selected sets."""
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import numpy as np

def compute_and_log_metrics(true_labels, pred_labels, num_classes=7):
    true_labels = np.array(true_labels, dtype=np.int64)
    pred_labels = np.array(pred_labels, dtype=np.int64)
    confusion_matrix_flat = np.bincount(
        np.ravel_multi_index((true_labels, pred_labels), (num_classes, num_classes)),
        minlength=num_classes*num_classes
    )
    confusion_matrix = confusion_matrix_flat.reshape(num_classes, num_classes)
    tp_per_class = np.diag(confusion_matrix)
    fp_per_class = np.sum(confusion_matrix, axis=0) - tp_per_class
    fn_per_class = np.sum(confusion_matrix, axis=1) - tp_per_class
    tn_per_class = np.sum(confusion_matrix) - (fp_per_class + fn_per_class + tp_per_class)
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        precision_per_class = tp_per_class / (tp_per_class + fp_per_class)

"""Traffic sequence storage, validation and CPU batch collation."""
import os
import numpy as np

class TrafficSequenceDatasetFromNPY:
    def __init__(self, data_file, labels_file, sequence_length=9):
        if not os.path.isfile(data_file):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Data file not found: {data_file}")
        if not os.path.isfile(labels_file):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Labels file not found: {labels_file}")
        self.sequences = np.load(data_file, allow_pickle=False)
        self.labels = np.load(labels_file, allow_pickle=False)
        self._validate(sequence_length)

    @classmethod
    def from_arrays(cls, sequences, labels, sequence_length=9):
        result = cls.__new__(cls)
        result.sequences = np.asarray(sequences, dtype=np.int64).reshape((-1,sequence_length,2))
        result.labels = np.asarray(labels, dtype=np.int64)
        result._validate(sequence_length)
        return result

    def _validate(self, sequence_length):
        if len(self.sequences) != len(self.labels):
            raise ValueError(f"Data length mismatch: {len(self.sequences)} vs {len(self.labels)}")
        self.sequences = self.sequences.astype(np.int64, copy=False)
        self.labels = self.labels.astype(np.int64, copy=False)
        if self.sequences.ndim != 3 or self.sequences.shape[1] != sequence_length:
            raise ValueError("Sequence length mismatch")
        if self.sequences.shape[2] != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"Feature dimension error: expected 2, got {self.sequences.shape[2]}")

    def __len__(self):
        return self.sequences.shape[0]

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        return self.sequences[index], self.labels[index]

def traffic_collate_fn_npy(batch):
    sequences, labels = zip(*batch)
    return np.stack(sequences, axis=0), np.asarray(labels,dtype=np.int64)

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right

def eligible_pairs(m):
    """Slot-major, then window-index, list of gated and in-range pairs."""
    buckets = [[] for _ in range(m.S)]
    for j in range(m.J):
        for s in range(m.lo[j], m.hi[j] + 1):
            buckets[s].append(j)
    pairs = []
    for s in range(m.S):
        for j in buckets[s]:
            pairs.append((s, j))
    return pairs


def arc_list(m, pairs, want):
    """Ordered (tail, head, lower, upper, cost) rows of the certificate net."""
    arcs = []
    for s in range(m.S):
        arcs.append((m.R, m.a[s], 0, m.I if s == 0 else m.refill[s], 0))
        arcs.append((m.a[s], m.b[s], 0, m.B, 0))
        if s + 1 < m.S:
            arcs.append((m.b[s], m.a[s + 1], 0, m.B, 0))
        arcs.append((m.b[s], m.e[s], 0, m.caps[s], 0))
    for s, j in pairs:
        window = m.windows[j]
        cost = (m.times[s] - window[1]) - m.value[j] * m.W
        arcs.append((m.e[s], m.w[j], 0, 1, cost))
    for j in range(m.J):
        arcs.append((m.w[j], m.z[m.windows[j][0]], 0, 1, 0))
    for f in range(m.F):
        arcs.append((m.z[f], m.flow_head[f], want[f], m.ceiling[f], 0))
    for i in range(m.G):
        arcs.append((m.h[i], m.group_head[i], 0, m.groups[i][1], 0))
    arcs.append((m.Z, m.R, 0, m.J, 0))
    return arcs


def flow_vector(m, meta, assign, want, extra=None):
    """Flow amount for every published arc, in published order."""
    g = meta['g']
    out = []
    for s in range(m.S):
        row = meta['tok'][s]
        out.append(g.cap[row[0] ^ 1])
        out.append(g.cap[row[1] ^ 1])
        if row[2] >= 0:
            out.append(g.cap[row[2] ^ 1])
        out.append(g.cap[row[3] ^ 1])
    for s, j in m.pairs:
        out.append(1 if assign[j] == s else 0)
    for j in range(m.J):
        out.append(1 if assign[j] >= 0 else 0)
    if extra is None:
        counts = [0] * m.F
        for j in range(m.J):
            if assign[j] >= 0:
                counts[m.windows[j][0]] += 1
    else:
        counts = extra
    out.extend(counts)
    for i in range(m.G):
        out.append(g.cap[meta['grp'][i] ^ 1])
    if extra is None:
        out.append(sum(counts))
    else:
        out.append(g.cap[meta['zr'] ^ 1])
    return out

    """Node set whose entering lower bounds exceed its leaving capacities."""
    meta = m.build('std', want)
    g = meta['g']
    max_flow(g, meta['ss'], meta['tt'])
    assign = m.decompose(meta)
    zflow = [g.cap[meta['z'][f] ^ 1] + want[f] for f in range(m.F)]
    values = flow_vector(m, meta, assign, want, zflow)
    values[-1] = g.cap[meta['zr'] ^ 1]
    arcs = m.arcs_plus
    size = m.K + 2

    adj = [[] for _ in range(size)]
    for index, (u, v, low, high, _) in enumerate(arcs):

        if amount < high:

        if amount > low:

    for f in range(m.F):
        used = g.cap[meta['ssa'][f] ^ 1]
        if used < want[f]:

        if used > 0:

        used = g.cap[meta['tta'][f] ^ 1]
        if used < want[f]:

        if used > 0:
            adj[m.K + 1].append(m.z[f])
    seen = [False] * size
    seen[ss] = True
    queue = [ss]
    for u in queue:
        for v in adj[u]:
            if not seen[v]:
                seen[v] = True
                queue.append(v)
    return [node for node in range(m.K) if seen[node]]


def plan(m):
    """Solve one epoch and emit its published result record."""
    m.pairs = eligible_pairs(m)
    low_index, high_index, _ = m.scan_coverage()
    levels = m.rset
    best = levels[low_index]
    want = m.wants(best)
    meta = m.optimise(want)
    assign = meta['assign']
    counts = [0] * m.F

    return {

        'age': age,

        'flow': flow,
        'potential': potential,
        'cut': cut,
        'counts': counts,
        'total': total,
        'coverage': best,
        'next': plus,
        'arcs': arcs,
        'meta': meta,
    }


def m_meta_unused(bonus, meta):

        self.G = len(case['groups'])
        self.times = [r[0] for r in case['slots']]
        self.caps = [r[1] for r in case['slots']]
        self.refill = [r[2] for r in case['slots']]
        self.B, self.I = case['bucket']
        self.W = 1 + self.J * self.times[-1]
        self.R, self.Z = 0, 1
        self.a = [2 + 3 * s for s in range(self.S)]
        self.b = [3 + 3 * s for s in range(self.S)]
        self.e = [4 + 3 * s for s in range(self.S)]
        base = 2 + 3 * self.S
        self.w = [base + j for j in range(self.J)]
        self.z = [base + self.J + f for f in range(self.F)]
        self.h = [base + self.J + self.F + g for g in range(self.G)]
        self.K = base + self.J + self.F + self.G

    def predict(self):
        windows = self.case['windows']
        if not windows:

            for j in range(self.J):

            arcs.append((self.a[s], self.b[s], 0, self.B, 0))
            if s + 1 < self.S:

def features(rng):
    return [[rng.randint(0, 1500), rng.randint(0, 2560)] for _ in range(9)]


def make_case(rng, big=False):
    S = rng.randint(1, 5 if not big else 12)
    J = rng.randint(0, 6 if not big else 40)
    F = rng.randint(1, 3 if not big else 6)
    G = rng.randint(0, 2 if not big else 4)
    t0 = rng.randint(0, 50)
    times = []
    cur = t0
    for _ in range(S):
        times.append(cur)
        cur += rng.randint(1, 30)
    caps = [rng.choice([0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5]) for _ in range(S)]
    refill = [0] + [rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 2, 3]) for _ in range(S - 1)]
    B = rng.randint(1, 6)
    I = rng.randint(0, B)
    groups = []
    for g in range(G):

    for f in range(F):

        flows.append([target, ceiling, group, rng.randint(0, 6)])

def best_plan(case, preds, thr):
    S = len(case['slots'])
    J = len(case['windows'])
    F = len(case['flows'])
    G = len(case['groups'])
    times = [r[0] for r in case['slots']]
    caps = [r[1] for r in case['slots']]
    refill = [r[2] for r in case['slots']]
    B, I = case['bucket']
    cv = case['class_values']
    values = [case['windows'][j][6] * cv[preds[j]] for j in range(J)]
    targets = [f[0] for f in case['flows']]
    children = {g: [] for g in range(G)}
    for g in range(G):
        p = case['groups'][g][0]
        if p >= 0:
            children[p].append(g)

    def group_total(counts, g):
        tot = sum(counts[f] for f in range(F) if case['flows'][f][2] == g)
        for c in children[g]:
            tot += group_total(counts, c)
        return tot

    opts = []
    for j in range(J):
        w = case['windows'][j]
        elig = []
        if w[5] < thr[j]:
            for s in range(S):
                if w[1] <= times[s] <= w[2]:
                    elig.append(s)
        opts.append(elig + [-1])
    best = None
    choice = [0] * J

    def rec(j, choice):
        nonlocal best
        if j == J:
            counts = [0] * F
            per = [0] * S
            u = 0
            a = 0
            for k in range(J):
                s = choice[k]
                if s >= 0:
                    counts[case['windows'][k][0]] += 1
                    per[s] += 1
                    u += values[k]
                    a += times[s] - case['windows'][k][1]
            for f in range(F):
                if counts[f] > case['flows'][f][1]:
                    return
            for g in range(G):
                if group_total(counts, g) > case['groups'][g][1]:
                    return
            carry = I
            for s in range(S):
                avail = I if s == 0 else min(carry + refill[s], B)
                if per[s] > min(caps[s], avail):
                    return
                carry = avail - per[s]
            cov = min([Fraction(1)] + [Fraction(counts[f], targets[f]) for f in range(F)])
            key = (cov, u, -a)
            if best is None or key > best[0]:
                best = (key, tuple(choice))
            return
        for s in opts[j]:
            choice[j] = s
            rec(j + 1, choice)
        choice[j] = 0

    rec(0, choice)
    (cov, u, a), pick = best
    return cov, u, -a, pick

"""Generate random requests, run the real candidate child, verify everything."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/dev')
import gen
import verify
import brute
import random


def run_candidate(raw):
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '/workspace/public_exec.py',
                           '/workspace/submission/main.py'], input=raw,
                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    return proc.stdout, proc.stderr, proc.returncode


def one(seed, big=False, do_brute=True, ncases=1):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    cases = [gen.make_case(rng, big) for _ in range(ncases)]
    req = {'version': 3, 'cases': cases}
    raw = json.dumps(req).encode()
    start = time.time()
    out, err, code = run_candidate(raw)
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    if code != 0:
        print('seed', seed, 'EXIT', code, err.decode()[:2000])
        return False
    try:
        resp = json.loads(out.decode())
    except Exception as exc:
        print('seed', seed, 'BAD JSON', exc, out[:400], err.decode()[:2000])
        return False
    if 'error' in resp:
        print('seed', seed, 'ERROR RESPONSE', resp, err.decode()[:500])
        return False
    verify.FAIL = []
    try:
        for cid, (case, result) in enumerate(zip(cases, resp['results'])):
            verify.verify_case(case, result, cid)
    except AssertionError as exc:
        print('seed', seed, 'VERIFY FAIL', exc)
        json.dump(req, open('/workspace/tmp/fail_%d.json' % seed, 'w'))
        open('/workspace/tmp/fail_%d.out' % seed, 'wb').write(out)
        return False
    if do_brute:
        for cid, (case, result) in enumerate(zip(cases, resp['results'])):
            cov, u, a, pick = brute.best_plan(case, result['predictions'], result['thresholds'])
            got = (verify.Fraction(result['ratio'][0], result['ratio'][1]), result['utility'], result['age'])
            if got != (cov, u, a):
                print('seed', seed, 'case', cid, 'BRUTE MISMATCH got', got, 'want', (cov, u, a))
                json.dump({'version': 3, 'cases': [case]}, open('/workspace/tmp/brute_%d_%d.json' % (seed, cid), 'w'))
                open('/workspace/tmp/brute_%d_%d.out' % (seed, cid), 'wb').write(json.dumps({'results': [result]}).encode())
                return False
    print('seed %d ok (%d cases, %.2fs, out %d bytes)' % (seed, len(cases), elapsed, len(out)))
    return True


def main():
    first = int(sys.argv[1])
    last = int(sys.argv[2])
    big = len(sys.argv) > 3 and sys.argv[3] == 'big'
    ncases = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 1

            ok = False
            break
    print('DONE', ok)
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

    windows = []

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""JSON entry point for the controller project."""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/vendor')
import json
import os

if '/workspace/native' not in os.environ.get('LD_LIBRARY_PATH', ''):
    # Defensive: the bundled native runtime libraries must be resolvable even
    # when the environment does not advertise them.
    import ctypes
    for _name in ('libz.so.1', 'libgcc_s.so.1', 'libstdc++.so.6'):
        _path = os.path.join('/workspace/native', _name)
        if os.path.exists(_path):
            try:
                ctypes.CDLL(_path, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
            except OSError:
                pass

from controller import run


def main():
    raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read(64 * 1024 * 1024)
    result = run(raw)
    out = sys.stdout
    out.write(json.dumps(result, separators=(',', ':')))
    out.write('\n')
    out.flush()
    sys.exit(0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Fast in-process campaign: random epoch -> plan -> verify -> brute force."""
import json

import time

sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/dev')

sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')

KINDS = ['std', 'frac', 'chain', 'loose', 'tight', 'starve']


def make(rng, kind):
    if kind == 'std':
        return gen.make_case(rng, False)
    if kind == 'frac':
        return gen2.frac_case(rng)
    if kind == 'chain':
        return gen2.chain_case(rng)
    return gen.make_case(rng, False, kind)


def main():
    first = int(sys.argv[1])
    last = int(sys.argv[2])
    kinds = sys.argv[3].split(',') if len(sys.argv) > 3 else KINDS
    fails = 0
    start = time.time()
    stats = {}
    for seed in range(first, last):
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        kind = kinds[seed % len(kinds)]
        case = make(rng, kind)
        raw = json.dumps({'version': 3, 'cases': [case]}).encode()
        out = controller.run(raw)
        if 'error' in out:
            print('seed', seed, kind, 'REJECTED valid input')
            json.dump(case, open('/workspace/tmp/camp_%d.json' % seed, 'w'))
            fails += 1
            continue
        res = out['results'][0]
        verify.FAIL = []
        try:
            cov, u, a = verify.verify_case(case, res, 0)
        except AssertionError as exc:
            print('seed', seed, kind, 'VERIFY', exc)
            json.dump(case, open('/workspace/tmp/camp_%d.json' % seed, 'w'))
            open('/workspace/tmp/camp_%d.out' % seed, 'w').write(json.dumps(res))
            fails += 1
            continue
        bcov, bu, ba, pick = brute.best_plan(case, res['predictions'], res['thresholds'])
        if (cov, u, a) != (bcov, bu, ba):
            print('seed', seed, kind, 'BRUTE got', (cov, u, a), 'want', (bcov, bu, ba))
            json.dump(case, open('/workspace/tmp/camp_%d.json' % seed, 'w'))
            open('/workspace/tmp/camp_%d.out' % seed, 'w').write(json.dumps(res))
            fails += 1
            continue
        stats[cov] = stats.get(cov, 0) + 1
    print('seeds %d..%d fails=%d time=%.1fs' % (first, last, fails, time.time() - start))
    print('coverage histogram:', sorted(((str(k), v) for k, v in stats.items()), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:12])
    return 1 if fails else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

    def __init__(self, n):

        self.nxt = []

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent reference planner on the uncompressed published network.

Feasibility by repeated max-flow over the public ratio set, optimality by
negative-cycle cancelling on the residual circulation. Deliberately naive;
used only to cross-check the submitted planner on small and medium epochs.

from fractions import Fraction


def ceil_frac(fr):
    return -((-fr.numerator) // fr.denominator)


class Net:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n
        self.to = []
        self.cap = []
        self.cost = []
        self.head = [-1] * n
        self.nxt = []

    def add(self, u, v, cap, cost=0):
        i = len(self.to)
        self.to.append(v)
        self.cap.append(cap)
        self.cost.append(cost)
        self.nxt.append(self.head[u])
        self.head[u] = i
        self.to.append(u)
        self.cap.append(0)
        self.cost.append(-cost)
        self.nxt.append(self.head[v])
        self.head[v] = i + 1
        return i


def dinic(g, s, t):
    n = g.n
    to = g.to
    cap = g.cap
    nxt = g.nxt
    head = g.head
    total = 0
    while True:
        level = [-1] * n
        level[s] = 0
        q = [s]
        for u in q:
            i = head[u]
            while i >= 0:
                if cap[i] > 0 and level[to[i]] < 0:
                    level[to[i]] = level[u] + 1
                    q.append(to[i])
                i = nxt[i]
        if level[t] < 0:
            return total
        it = head[:]

        def dfs(u, push):
            if u == t:
                return push
            i = it[u]
            while i >= 0:
                c = cap[i]
                if c > 0 and level[to[i]] == level[u] + 1:
                    d = dfs(to[i], min(push, c))
                    if d:
                        cap[i] -= d
                        cap[i ^ 1] += d
                        return d
                i = nxt[i]
                it[i] = i
            return 0

        while True:
            f = dfs(s, 1 << 60)
            if not f:
                break
            total += f


def build(case, preds, thr, want, with_cost):
    S = len(case['slots'])
    J = len(case['windows'])
    F = len(case['flows'])
    G = len(case['groups'])
    times = [r[0] for r in case['slots']]
    caps = [r[1] for r in case['slots']]
    refill = [r[2] for r in case['slots']]
    B, I = case['bucket']
    W = 1 + J * times[-1]
    cv = case['class_values']
    value = [case['windows'][j][6] * cv[preds[j]] for j in range(J)]
    R, Z = 0, 1
    a = [2 + 3 * s for s in range(S)]
    b = [3 + 3 * s for s in range(S)]
    e = [4 + 3 * s for s in range(S)]
    base = 2 + 3 * S
    w = [base + j for j in range(J)]
    z = [base + J + f for f in range(F)]
    h = [base + J + F + g for g in range(G)]
    K = base + J + F + G
    ss, tt = K, K + 1
    g = Net(K + 2)
    for s in range(S):
        g.add(R, a[s], I if s == 0 else refill[s])
        g.add(a[s], b[s], B)
        if s + 1 < S:

    pairs = []

    for gi in range(G):

    g.add(Z, R, J)
    for f in range(F):

        g.add(ss, head, want[f])
        g.add(z[f], tt, want[f])
    return g, ss, tt, sum(want), pairs, value, times, first_pair_arc


def cancel_cycles(g, rounds=20000):
    n = g.n

            g.cap[i ^ 1] += width

    S = len(case['slots'])
    J = len(case['windows'])
    F = len(case['flows'])

    for level in rset:

        children = [[] for _ in range(count)]

        order = []
        stack = roots[:]

            order.append(node)

        order.reverse()
        return order

        tok = []
        for s in range(self.S):

def infeasibility_cut(m, want, arcs):
    """Node set whose entering lower bounds exceed its leaving capacities."""
    meta = m.build('std', want)
    g = meta['g']
    max_flow(g, meta['ss'], meta['tt'])
    assign = m.decompose(meta)
    zflow = [g.cap[meta['z'][f] ^ 1] + want[f] for f in range(m.F)]
    values = flow_vector(m, meta, assign, want, zflow)
    size = m.K + 2
    ss = m.K
    adj = [[] for _ in range(size)]
    for index, (u, v, low, high, _) in enumerate(arcs):
        amount = values[index]
        if amount < high:
            adj[u].append(v)
        if amount > low:
            adj[v].append(u)
    for f in range(m.F):
        used = g.cap[meta['ssa'][f] ^ 1]
        if used < want[f]:
            adj[ss].append(m.flow_head[f])
        if used > 0:
            adj[m.flow_head[f]].append(ss)
        used = g.cap[meta['tta'][f] ^ 1]
        if used < want[f]:
            adj[m.z[f]].append(m.K + 1)
        if used > 0:
            adj[m.K + 1].append(m.z[f])
    seen = [False] * size
    seen[ss] = True
    queue = [ss]
    for u in queue:
        for v in adj[u]:
            if not seen[v]:
                seen[v] = True
                queue.append(v)
    return [node for node in range(m.K) if seen[node]]


def plan(m):
    """Solve one epoch and emit its published planning record."""
    m.pairs = eligible_pairs(m)
    levels = m.rset
    low_index, high_index, _ = m.scan_coverage()
    best = levels[low_index]
    want = m.wants(best)
    meta = m.optimise(want)
    assign = meta['assign']
    counts = [0] * m.F
    utility = 0
    age = 0
    for j in range(m.J):
        s = assign[j]
        if s >= 0:
            counts[m.windows[j][0]] += 1
            utility += m.value[j]
            age += m.times[s] - m.windows[j][1]
    g = meta['g']
    for f in range(m.F):
        arc = meta['bonus'][f]
        if arc >= 0 and g.cap[arc ^ 1] != want[f]:
            raise AssertionError('coverage lower bound not met')
    total = sum(counts)
    if total != meta['total']:
        raise AssertionError('token accounting mismatch')
    arcs = arc_list(m, m.pairs, want)
    flow = flow_vector(m, meta, assign, want)
    flow[-1] = total
    if high_index < len(levels):
        plus = levels[high_index]
        want_plus = m.wants(plus)
        cut = infeasibility_cut(m, want_plus, arc_list(m, m.pairs, want_plus))
    else:
        cut = None
    return {
        'utility': utility,
        'age': age,
        'ratio': [best.numerator, best.denominator],
        'assignment': assign,
        'flow': flow,
        'potential': meta['pi'][:m.K],
        'cut': cut,
        'coverage': best,
        'counts': counts,
        'arcs': arcs,
        'want': want,
    }

class Model:
    """One parsed epoch with derived planning data and node coordinates."""

    def __init__(self, case, predictions, thresholds):
        self.class_values = case['class_values']
        self.B = case['bucket'][0]
        self.I = case['bucket'][1]
        slots = case['slots']
        self.S = len(slots)
        self.times = [row[0] for row in slots]
        self.caps = [row[1] for row in slots]
        self.refill = [row[2] for row in slots]
        self.flows = case['flows']
        self.F = len(self.flows)
        self.groups = case['groups']
        self.G = len(self.groups)
        self.windows = case['windows']
        self.J = len(self.windows)
        self.predictions = predictions
        self.thresholds = thresholds
        S, J, F, G = self.S, self.J, self.F, self.G
        self.W = 1 + J * self.times[-1]
        self.value = [self.windows[j][6] * self.class_values[predictions[j]]
                      for j in range(J)]
        times = self.times
        self.lo = [0] * J
        self.hi = [-1] * J
        for j, window in enumerate(self.windows):
            if window[5] < thresholds[j]:
                left = bisect_left(times, window[1])
                right = bisect_right(times, window[2]) - 1
                if left <= right:
                    self.lo[j] = left
                    self.hi[j] = right
        n0 = 1
        while n0 < S:
            n0 <<= 1
        self.n0 = n0
        self.tree_n = 2 * n0 - 1
        self.covers = []
        for j in range(J):
            lo = self.lo[j]
            hi = self.hi[j]
            if lo > hi:
                self.covers.append(())
                continue
            found = []
            left = lo + n0
            right = hi + n0 + 1
            while left < right:
                if left & 1:
                    found.append(left)
                    left += 1
                if right & 1:
                    right -= 1
                    found.append(right)
                left >>= 1
                right >>= 1
            self.covers.append(tuple(found))
        self.R = 0
        self.Z = 1
        self.a = [2 + 3 * s for s in range(S)]
        self.b = [3 + 3 * s for s in range(S)]
        self.e = [4 + 3 * s for s in range(S)]
        base = 2 + 3 * S
        self.w = [base + j for j in range(J)]
        self.z = [base + J + f for f in range(F)]
        self.h = [base + J + F + g for g in range(G)]
